draft.note_text:
Subjective: Male pt with low back pain since yesterday. Was raking leaves and felt fine; about 2 hrs later back started tightening up, with pins and needles in right foot. One similar episode about 3 yrs ago, resolved after a day. Tried ice and 2 Advil without relief. Hot shower helped; feels a little better sitting. Normally does no physical activity. Partner present: reports pain looks worse when he stands back up from bending than on bending over; is worried because his pain tolerance is high; requests MRI now. Has not taken meloxicam before.
Objective: Low back: some pain on flexion, no pain on extension per pt. Pain to palpation around L5. Dorsiflexion normal. Pulses equal in all extremities. Tingling reported in right leg. Low back x-ray today: normal.
Assessment: Probable low back sprain.
Plan: Rest. Meloxicam prescribed. PT referral for stretches and exercises. Pt to message if not improving. Partner's request for immediate MRI discussed; agreed to give it 2 weeks, then call back and MRI will be arranged if still not improving.

The patient has not taken meloxicam before.
The patient's partner notes that he has a high pain tolerance and would not normally complain, and that this episode is really painful.
On examination, the patient localized the tingling sensation to his right leg.
